 3 tat, tena, tasmAt, tataH ‘as-s(o)’ yaTA-taTA; ‘s(o) that’ taTA-yaTA; ‘s(o) and so’ amuka (kI f.); mayA hyamukasUnunA liKitaM hyamu-kena (Y. ii. 88) ‘written by me s(o) and s(o), the son of s(o) and s(o)’; ‘s(o)-called’ nAma, nAman in comp.; ‘s(o) far’ etAvat, etadavaDi; etAvatparyaMtaM; ‘s(o) far as’ tAvat, oft. ex. by iti; See As; ‘s(o) forth’ ityAdi, evamAdi; ‘s(o) long’ etA-vatkAlaM yAvat, iyato divasAn, iyaMtaM kAlaM; ‘s(o) long as’ yAvat-tAvat; ‘s(o) many’ iyat, etAvat, ‘as many’, ‘s(o) many’ yAvat-tAvat; ‘s(o) much’ (adv.) tAdfk; Idfk, taTA; (a.) etAvat iyat; ‘s(o) that’ yena, yaTA; ‘s(o) then’ evaM tarhi, etAvatA, evaM ca; ‘s(o) much as’ api, api tAvat; ‘could not s(o) much as wet the tip of his bill’ caMcvagramapi tAvat jalaklinnaM kartuM nASakat.
